guarantees.claim: When fifo_valid_i, fifo_ready_o, and kmac_en_i are all true, the FSM state must be StKmacMsg.

assumptions.claim: kmac_en_i changes only when state is Idle or TerminalError.
assumptions.risk: Toggling enable during active operation could cause state corruption or incomplete processing.

assumptions.claim: mode_i changes only when state is Idle or TerminalError.
assumptions.risk: Mode alteration mid-operation may lead to incorrect algorithm execution or security downgrade.

assumptions.claim: strength_i changes only when state is Idle, TerminalError, or the previous state was Idle.
assumptions.risk: Strength adjustment during operation could violate security requirements or cause faulty processing.

assumptions.claim: When key_valid_i is asserted (and not just newly asserted), key_len_i must remain stable.
assumptions.risk: Key length change after validation could cause incorrect key loading and compromise cryptographic operations.

assumptions.claim: When key_valid_i is asserted (and not just newly asserted), key_data_i must remain stable.
assumptions.risk: Key material change during valid window could leak or corrupt secret data.

assumptions.claim: When state is StKmacMsg and process_latched is high, process_latched must become low in the next cycle.
assumptions.risk: If process_latched stays high, it may indicate a stuck handshake, stalling the pipeline.

uncertain_points.claim: The design assumes configuration inputs (kmac_en_i, mode_i, strength_i, key_len_i, key_data_i) are stable outside idle/error states, but no local enforcement is visible in this chunk; an adversary that drives these inputs could change them mid-operation, leading to security downgrade or secret leakage.
uncertain_points.cond: Any violation of the stability assumptions
uncertain_points.risk: Secret exposure or algorithm‑strength bypass if an attacker can inject timing‑uncorrelated config changes.
